Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the InnoMed Devices Q1 FY2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Maria Chen, CFO; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. InnoMed Devices achieved record results this Q1, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio and our commitment to innovation.

Today, I will cover eight key aspects of our performance:
1. Strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter
2. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary
3. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
4. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives
5. Gross margin trends and supply chain commentary
6. Overall performance highlights and key achievements
7. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
8. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends

Maria will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Raj will update us on our technology advancements, and Tom will discuss our market strategies. We'll then conclude with a Q&A session.

Now, let's get started with strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter.

As we wrap up a solid Q1 with 12% year-over-year revenue growth to $1.2 billion—driven by 18% procedural growth in our structural heart franchise and resilient orthopedics performance amid softer elective volumes—our playbook remains centered on three pillars: accelerating innovation in high-growth adjacencies, optimizing our global footprint for margin expansion, and fortifying our balance sheet for disciplined capital deployment. These initiatives position InnoMed Devices to capture share in a $550 billion TAM that's growing at 5.5% CAGR through 2030, fueled by aging demographics, rising chronic disease prevalence, and the shift to value-based care.

First, we're doubling down on our next-generation robotics platform, building on the momentum from our InnoBot Xi system, which incorporates proprietary AI-driven haptic feedback for precision in complex neurovascular procedures—much like Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci but tailored for our needs. In Q1, we saw 25% sequential adoption growth in U.S. hybrid ORs, with ASPs holding firm at $1.8 million per unit despite competitive pricing from Medtronic's Hugo RAS. For Q2, we expect FDA 510(k) clearance for our AI-augmented electrophysiology module by mid-quarter, targeting a $4.5 billion addressable market in AFib ablations where procedural volumes are up 15% YoY per Society of Thoracic Surgeons data. We'll invest $75 million—or 6% of projected Q2 revenue—in clinical trials across 20 sites, aiming for 30% YoY growth in robotics revenue to $180 million. Real-world evidence from over 5,000 cases shows a 22% reduction in procedure times and 18% lower complication rates versus legacy systems, directly supporting CMS reimbursement under the IPPS updates.

Second, geopolitically, we're navigating headwinds like EU MDR compliance delays—now pushing some legacy approvals into H2—but leaning into tailwinds in APAC and LATAM. The U.S. remains our bedrock at 65% of revenue, with Q1 orthopedics up 9% on strong momentum from our Triad knee implant, outpacing Stryker's Mako in same-day discharge rates at 85% versus the market's 72%. For Q2, we're prioritizing China, where NMPA approval for our next-gen TAVR valve, InnoValve Pro, is on track for June, tapping a $2.2 billion market growing 22% CAGR amid 1.4 million annual aortic stenosis cases. We'll deploy 50 sales reps and partner with local CROs like WuXi AppTec for post-market surveillance, forecasting 35% YoY growth to $120 million in Greater China revenue. In EMEA, expect softer 5-7% growth due to NHS backlogs, offset by a new distribution pact with Fresenius Medical Care for our renal access portfolio, aiming to lift dialysis catheter share to 15% from 11%. Emerging markets like India and Brazil get $20 million in localized manufacturing investments to counter 10-12% import duties, driving organic growth to 14% internationally.

Third, inflationary pressures on titanium and nitinol alloys—up 8% since Q4—are real, but our Q1 gross margin of 65.2% reflects proactive hedging and vertical integration. In Q2, we'll execute Phase 2 of our Resilient MedChain initiative: shifting 25% of structural heart component production from single-source Taiwan suppliers to dual-sourced facilities in Mexico and Ireland, mitigating Red Sea disruptions that inflated ocean freight 15% last quarter. This supports our guide for flat-to-up 2% ASPs amid pricing discipline. On SG&A, we're targeting $50 million in savings via AI-optimized field force deployment—leveraging Salesforce Health Cloud to boost rep productivity 12%—while R&D efficiency hits 11.5% of sales through cross-franchise synergies, like applying our neuromodulation algorithms to diabetes tech similar to Abbott's FreeStyle Libre evolutions. Sustainability is non-negotiable: Q2 marks full ISO 14001 certification for 80% of sites, aligning with EU Green Deal mandates and unlocking preferred vendor status with payers like UnitedHealth.

Finally, with $2.8 billion in cash and a net leverage of 1.8x, we're primed for bolt-ons. Top of mind: tuck-in opportunities in digital therapeutics, scanning the horizon post-Nexus Neuro's recent $300 million raise. We've allocated $400 million for FY25 M&A, with Q2 scouting three targets in wearables for remote patient monitoring—a $15 billion market per IQVIA—to complement our CardioPatch ECG sensor, which hit 500k units shipped in Q1. Share repurchases continue at $100 million quarterly, with 2.1% yield post our recent authorization.

Now, let's talk about procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

Global procedure volumes grew 14% year-over-year and 6% sequentially in Q1, marking our fifth straight quarter of double-digit organic growth. This exceeded our internal expectations and reflects a robust snapback in elective procedures, now running at 95% of pre-pandemic levels globally—up from 82% a year ago. To put this in context, our baseline 2019 Q1 volumes serve as the gold standard, and we're now at 108% of that benchmark on an adjusted basis, excluding pandemic-related distortions like deferred cases and supply chain bottlenecks.

Our Cardiovascular business led with 17% YoY volume growth. TAVR procedures, powered by our next-gen Acuity Ultra valve—launched in the US and EU earlier this year—surged 22%, capturing 2 points of share from competitors like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien platform. We're seeing strong penetration in intermediate- and high-risk patients, with average procedure times down 15% thanks to our integrated imaging suite, which enhances procedural efficiency and reduces fluoroscopy exposure. PCI volumes were up 12%, buoyed by our Elute Pro drug-eluting stents, which benefited from expanded indications for complex bifurcations and CTOs—chronic total occlusions—amid rising CAD prevalence.

In Orthopedics, volumes expanded 11% YoY, driven by a 16% uptick in robotic-assisted knee and hip replacements using our Mako platform, with proprietary AI-driven planning algorithms that improved implant accuracy to 98% in our latest clinical data—akin to Stryker's ecosystem. Hip procedures outperformed at 14% growth, reflecting pent-up demand from aging demographics; we're now at 112% of 2019 levels here. Shoulder and spine cases grew more modestly at 8%, tempered by lingering surgeon backlogs, but our new Trinity cementless stem is gaining traction with early adopters.

Neuromodulation rounded out at 9% YoY growth, with deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's up 13% on the back of our ReviX platform's directional leads, which offer 30% better symptom control per our INSIDE registry data. Pain management DBS volumes were flat sequentially due to seasonal elective slowdowns but remain on a 10% trajectory.

Regionally, the US was the powerhouse at 16% YoY volume growth, fueled by CMS reimbursement tailwinds for TAVR under the TAVR 2.0 pathway and our success in Medicare Advantage plans, where we've secured preferred status with UnitedHealth and Humana. Hospital utilization rates hit 92% of pre-COVID peaks, with case mix indices up 4% as facilities prioritize high-acuity procedures. Europe lagged at 10% growth, held back by NICE guidelines in the UK delaying TAVR expansions and softer German DRG reimbursements, but we're optimistic with our CE Mark for the Acuity Ultra now live in 12 countries. ASPAC was a bright spot at 18% YoY, led by China where NMPA approvals for our Mako robotics drove 25% knee volume growth amid a 20% national rise in arthroplasty demand. Emerging markets like Brazil and India contributed 15% growth, supported by our low-cost Trinity implants tailored for price-sensitive volumes.

The sector is firmly in Phase 3 of the post-COVID cycle: full elective normalization coupled with structural tailwinds. We're modeling global procedure growth of 8-10% in FY25, aligning with consensus from firms like Leerink and JPMorgan, but with upside from obesity-related interventions—our GLP-1 tie-ins for bariatric device combos position us well here. Supply chain resilience has been critical; our US manufacturing ramp-up reduced lead times for stents by 40%, enabling just-in-time delivery to IDNs like HCA and Tenet.

Strategically, we're leaning into digital ecosystem integration: Our Procedure Analytics Platform, now live in 40% of US sites, uses real-time OR data to optimize scheduling, boosting utilization by 12% for partners. We're accelerating innovation velocity—five new 510(k)s filed in Q1, including a bioresorbable scaffold for peripheral artery disease to address the $2B PAD market underserved by Boston Scientific's Eluvia. M&A adjacency: Our bolt-on acquisition of NeuroStim last quarter adds spinal cord stim tech, instantly lifting neuromod volumes by 5% through cross-selling.

Looking forward, we see Q2 volumes at 12-15% YoY, with risks skewed to the upside from US midterms stabilizing reimbursement and China's 14th Five-Year Plan emphasizing robotics. Pricing held firm at +1% organic, reflecting our VBP wins and portfolio premiumization.

Moving on to SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

SG&A expenses came in at $285 million for Q1, up just 2% year-over-year on a reported basis, but flat sequentially from Q4. As a percentage of revenue, we improved to 26.2%—a 140 basis point enhancement from 27.6% in Q1 last year and our best quarterly performance since pre-pandemic levels. This drove $18 million in sequential efficiencies, contributing roughly 50 basis points to our adjusted operating margin expansion to 22.4%. On a full-year basis, we're tracking toward $1.15 billion in total SG&A, implying a leverage of about 120 basis points versus FY24, with a target SG&A-to-revenue ratio of 25.5% to 26% by year-end.

Selling expenses—which make up 55% of our SG&A—rose only 1% YoY to $157 million, despite a 9% revenue increase in our core segments like endovascular robotics and TAVR valves. This reflects robust sales force productivity gains, where we've optimized our 2,800-strong field team through data-driven territory realignments and digital enablement. Our rep-to-procedure ratio improved 12% YoY, mirroring best practices at peers like Intuitive Surgical with their da Vinci Xi platform, where surgeon utilization metrics are paramount. We rolled out Salesforce Health Cloud integrated with our proprietary AI-powered procedure forecasting tool, which has boosted virtual case coverage by 35%, reducing travel costs by $12 million YoY—critical as fuel and lodging inflation lingers at 5-7%.

On the G&A side, expenses declined 4% YoY to $128 million, driven by aggressive shared services optimization. We've centralized back-office functions in our Manila and Hyderabad hubs, capturing $22 million in annualized savings from procure-to-pay automation via SAP Ariba and robotic process automation bots handling 70% of invoice processing. This zero-based budgeting approach—now in its third year—has yielded a 15% reduction in indirect spend, including professional fees and IT infrastructure, without compromising our FDA 21 CFR Part 11 compliance or ISO 13485 quality standards.

Regionally, our efforts are tailored. In the U.S., which accounts for 52% of SG&A, we navigated the 2.8% MPFS cut by enhancing value-based selling for our next-gen drug-eluting stents, similar to Boston Scientific's Synergy platform. This shifted focus from volume to outcomes data, improving customer acquisition cost by 18% in hospital IDNs like HCA and Kaiser. Europe, at 28% of spend, benefited from £10 million in efficiencies from harmonizing our 12-country sales ops post-Brexit, leveraging the EU MDR transition to consolidate distributor partnerships—key as NICE guidelines tighten on electrophysiology devices. In Asia-Pacific, our fastest-growing region at 22% SG&A allocation, we gained 25 basis points of leverage through localized digital training platforms for products like our PCI balloons, offsetting China's NRDL pricing pressures while ramping 30% procedure growth in India.

These gains are embedded in our Efficiency 2.0 roadmap, including digitization like AI chatbots for surgeon KOL engagement, piloted on our MitraClip-like transcatheter mitral valve repair system; portfolio rationalization, divesting low-margin legacy orthopedics to focus on $5B+ TAM opportunities in neuromodulation; and M&A synergy capture, where post our robotic-assisted endoscopy firm acquisition, we've realized 60% of the $40 million cost synergies ahead of schedule. Looking ahead, we expect another 100-150 basis points of SG&A leverage in FY25, supported by GenAI pilots in contract lifecycle management that could unlock an additional $15-20 million.

Next, impact of pricing and cost management initiatives.

The medical devices sector has faced persistent headwinds—Medicare price transparency rules, intensifying GPO negotiations with players like Vizient and Premier, and inflationary pressures on raw materials like titanium alloys and medical-grade polymers. Yet, through disciplined execution, these initiatives drove a 320 basis point expansion in our adjusted gross margin to 67.8%, up from 64.6% a year ago, while contributing approximately $185 million to incremental EBITDA.

Our pricing strategy remains anchored in demonstrating superior clinical outcomes and economic value, aligning with value-based care models. In the US, where we derive 52% of revenue, we successfully renewed contracts covering 65% of our hospital volumes with key GPOs, securing an average 2.8% ASP uplift—our strongest in three years. This was led by our Cardiovascular franchise, including our next-gen TAVR valves like the EchoFlow platform, which outperformed competitors like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien in bundled payment pilots, justifying a 4.1% price premium based on reduced readmission rates of 12% versus the market average.

Ex-US, performance was mixed but resilient. In Europe (28% of revenue), we navigated stringent HTA scrutiny from bodies like NICE in the UK and IQWiG in Germany, maintaining flat-to-1% ASP erosion through outcome-based pricing clauses tied to our neuromodulation leads, similar to Medtronic's Intellis platform. Notably, our orthopedic portfolio—hip and knee implants under the FlexiBone brand—benefited from favorable tender wins in Italy and Spain, offsetting a 1.5% headwind from France's reformed reimbursement tariffs. In emerging markets (20% of revenue), particularly China via our JV with a local partner akin to MicroPort, we accepted modest 3% ASP compression in exchange for 15% unit volume growth, capitalizing on the National Reimbursement Drug List expansions for high-acuity devices.

Overall, pricing realization exceeded our guidance by 50 basis points, adding $112 million to topline versus our base case, with a favorable product mix shift—higher-margin robotics and minimally invasive devices now at 42% of mix, up from 38%.

Complementing pricing, our cost initiatives yielded $210 million in run-rate savings, with 70% flowing directly to the bottom line. On COGS, which represents 32% of revenue, we achieved a 6.2% reduction through supply chain optimization: consolidating our top 20 suppliers by 15%, reducing variability in specialty resins and electronic components post-semiconductor shortages; localization efforts in Mexico and Vietnam cut ocean freight costs by 22%, shielding us from Red Sea disruptions; manufacturing productivity via Lean Six Sigma programs across our 14 global plants reduced defects by 18% to 0.4% yield loss, while Industry 4.0 investments boosted throughput 12%; and R&D portfolio rationalization divested two underperforming assets, pruning spend to 11.2% of revenue without sacrificing innovation.

On OpEx, SG&A deleveraged 210 bps to 24.5% of revenue through digital tools like Salesforce Health Cloud for sales force automation, cutting field rep travel 30%, and selective offshoring saving $42 million.

By segment: Cardiovascular gross margins expanded 410 bps to 70.2% on pricing wins and scale; Orthopedics gained 280 bps via raw material hedges; Diabetes Care CGMs held steady despite biosensor chip volatility. Regionally, US margins hit 69.5% (+350 bps), Europe 66% (+200 bps), APAC 64% (+150 bps).

These initiatives are embedded in our ValueMax framework, emphasizing total cost of ownership—e.g., our 5-year TCO models showing 18% savings versus legacy products from J&J's DePuy line. We expect continued 1.5-2% ASP growth in FY25, with cost savings ramping to $250 million run-rate, targeting 69% gross margins.

Then, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary.

We delivered a strong quarter with GAAP gross margin of 68.2%, up 210 basis points sequentially from Q4 last year and 140 basis points year-over-year. This marks the third consecutive quarter of expansion, bringing our trailing four-quarter average to 67.5%. Non-GAAP gross margin, excluding certain one-time charges related to EU MDR remediation, came in at 69.4%.

Favorable product mix was the largest contributor, accounting for roughly 160 basis points. Our consumables and disposables business—single-use guidewires, balloon catheters, and implant kits—now represents 62% of total revenue, up from 58% a year ago. These high-margin categories, with blends north of 75%, benefited from strong procedural growth in electrophysiology and TAVR procedures, where we're gaining share against incumbents like Medtronic's CoreValve and Abbott's Navitor. Capital equipment, like our next-gen imaging cath lab systems, pulled the blend down slightly due to a $45 million shipment of lower-margin systems to emerging markets, but ASPs held firm at $1.2 million per unit.

Manufacturing efficiencies added about 100 basis points. We've realized $28 million in annualized savings from our Smart Factory initiative, leveraging Industry 4.0 tech—AI-driven predictive maintenance on CNC machining lines for orthopedic titanium implants and robotic automation in sterile packaging. This reduced scrap rates by 18% in our Heredia, Costa Rica facility and boosted yields on bioresorbable scaffolds from 82% to 91%. Raw material costs remain a headwind; medical-grade polycarbonate resins and noble metals like platinum-iridium for pacemaker leads are up 12-15% YoY due to petrochemical inflation and supply constraints from Russia's export curbs.

Regionally, U.S. margins expanded to 71% on better reimbursement under CMS APC updates for our cardiology suite, EMEA held at 65% amid pricing pressure from UK's HTA bodies and Germany's NUB negotiations, APAC saw margins dip to 62% due to volume discounts in China for OrthoMax hip systems, but we're mitigating with localized production in Suzhou.

We expect Q2 gross margins of 68.5-69.5%, with full-year guidance of 68-69%, implying 100-150 basis points of YoY expansion, assuming stable FX and moderating input costs. Key levers include scaling vertical integration in polymer extrusion, insourcing 30% of catheter shafts by year-end, and accelerating adoption of our premium FlexiFlow Ultra stent at 78% margins versus 72% for standard.

On supply chain, Days Inventory Outstanding improved to 142 days from 158 last quarter. Lead times for critical components normalized: semiconductor ASICs for imaging Doppler probes back to 16 weeks from 32, thanks to dual-sourcing from TSMC and a new U.S. partner under CHIPS Act incentives. Multi-year contracts for 70% of nitinol supply—with U.S. and Mexico suppliers—insulate from China's 60% global dominance.

Geopolitical risks persist: Red Sea disruptions extended ocean freight from Asia by 10-14 days, impacting 15% of imports like rare earth neodymium for MRI-compatible devices. U.S. cleanroom labor shortages pushed contract manufacturing costs up 8%, so we're investing $50 million in automation at our Galway, Ireland hub.

We're advancing supplier diversification, onboarding three new vendors for medical-grade silicones, reducing single-source exposure from 22% to 14%; digital supply chain twin via SAP S/4HANA for real-time disruption modeling; and sustainability, transitioning 40% of packaging to recycled PET by Q4.

Then, overall performance highlights and key achievements.

Total revenue reached $875 million, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially—well ahead of our $840-855 million guidance midpoint. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, driven by procedural volume recovery, pricing discipline, and share gains in high-margin consumables. Cardiovascular revenue surged 22% to $480 million, fueled by robust uptake of our InnoStent Prime series, capturing an additional 250 basis points of U.S. market share to 14.5% per Millennium Research. Orthopedics grew 12% to $250 million, with OrthoBot NX posting 35% unit growth amid 15% industry-wide robotic procedures. Neuromodulation hit $145 million, up 16%, from expanded indications for ReNeuve DBS leads in Parkinson's and chronic migraine.

Adjusted non-GAAP EPS was $1.42, a 24% increase YoY and $0.08 above consensus—our strongest beat in two years. Gross margins expanded 220 basis points to 68.5% thanks to efficiencies at our Greenville, South Carolina facility, ramped to 85% utilization. Operating margins hit 28.2%, up from 25.1%, with SG&A growing just 10% despite $25 million R&D investments.

Operationally, regulatory wins: FDA 510(k) and CE Mark for CardioFlow TAVR valve, with 95% procedural success and 20% reduced paravalvular leak vs. Sapien 3, targeting $150 million FY25 revenue. In orthopedics, BioFix Advance ACL system got Breakthrough Device Designation, reducing revisions by 30%.

Regionally broad-based: U.S. 20% growth (55% of revenue), outpacing 12% medtech per Evaluate MedTech; Europe 14% in constant currency (25%); APAC 28%, China 35% via JV with Sinomed Tech; emerging markets 8% organic.

Strategically, amid aging demographics driving 6-8% procedural growth, shift to minimally invasive/digital therapies, and value-based care: $300 million AI roadmap for imaging anomaly detection (15% faster procedures); supply chain diversification of 40% nitinol sourcing; pipeline first patients dosed in NeuroPulse RF ablation for AFib ($4B TAM); $220 million tuck-in of Ortho Dynamics adding sports med SKUs with 20% accretion.

We're raising FY25 guidance: revenue $3.55-3.65 billion (16-19% growth); adjusted EPS $5.75-5.90.

Then, organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Organic revenue performance came in at 9.2% year-over-year growth on constant currency—sixth straight quarter of double-digit ex-FX in key segments. Excluding NeuroStim acquisition and FX headwinds (150 bps off reported).

Cardiovascular (42% or $1.82B): 12.8% organic, structural heart 18.5% on VitalFlow TAVR (22% U.S. share, ORBIT-3 data); Watchman FLX up 25% on Medicare; CRM 10.2% on Micra AV (150k implants); margins 68%.

Orthopedics & Spine (28% or $1.21B): 7.4%, hips 14% on Triad Cementless (15% lower revisions per AJRR); spine flat on China pricing, Peregrine MIS screws launching; margins 62%.

Advanced Surgical Technologies (18% or $785M): 11.1%, endoscopy 15% on SpyGlass DS (28% U.S. ERCP); robotics 22% on VitalBot (20k procedures); margins 65%.

Diabetes & Patient Monitoring (12% or $512M): 6.9%, CGM 12% on VitalSense 7-day (Roche partnerships); monitoring 3%; margins 60%.

Geography: U.S. (58% or $2.51B) 10.5%, CMS IPPS tailwinds, ASC ortho 35%; EMEA (22% or $952M) 8.1%, Germany/UK 12%; APAC (14% or $606M) 13.2%, China 18%; Rest of World (6% or $259M) 7.8%.

Affirming Innovate to Penetrate: 12.5% R&D (up from 11.2%), 150 bps share gains per IQVIA; tailwinds from 65+ population growth, value-based care for 8-10% organic FY25.

Finally, capital equipment vs consumables mix trends.

Capital equipment: high-value durables like PrecisionNav robotics, EchoScan ultrasound, NeuroStim generators (long sales cycles, annuity via consumables—catheters, ablation tips, guidewires, implants). Q1 revenue $2.8B, up 11% organic. Consumables 72% ($2.02B, +14%); capital 28% ($780M, +5%). 200 bps sequential shift to consumables (from 70/30), 400 bps YoY (from 68/32); T12M 71% consumables.

Installed base +9% to 18,500 systems, utilization 72% (150 bps up); robotics PrecisionNav +22% procedures, ASP $1,450/kit (+2%). Capital ASP $2.1M (-1%), 1,200 units.

U.S. (52%) consumables 78% (+4% YoY), CMS APC $4,200 for neuromod, electrophysiology +15%; Europe (28%) 65/35, capital +8% tenders; APAC (15%) 68/32 (+500 bps), China VBP normalized +20% consumables.

Initiatives: PrecisionNav 2.0 AI upgrade +17% efficiency; 85% single-use lock-in; $150M modular upgrades. Consumables 68% margins vs capital 52%, blended 64% (+150 bps). Recurring covers 115% OpEx; CardioFlow add $300M consumables. Expect 74% consumables by 2025 YE, FY25 $11.2-11.5B, EPS $8.45-8.65.

I will now turn the call over to Maria for a review of our financial results.

Maria Chen:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered exceptional financial performance this quarter. Revenue hit $1.2 billion, up 12% YoY, with organic growth of 9.2% driven by procedural strength across segments. Gross margins expanded to 68.2% GAAP, 69.4% non-GAAP, fueled by mix shift to 72% consumables, pricing +2.8% in US, and $210M cost savings. SG&A leveraged to 26.2%, operating margins to 28.2%, adjusted EPS $1.42 beating consensus. Balance sheet strong at $2.8B cash, 1.8x net leverage. FY25 guidance raised: revenue $3.55-3.65B (16-19% growth), EPS $5.75-5.90, gross margins 68-69%, FCF conversion >90%. Q2: $1.25-1.30B revenue (11-14% YoY), EPS $1.45-1.55.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj for an update on our product pipeline.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Maria. We are excited about the progress we are making in our technology roadmap. Our latest innovation, InnoBot Xi, is poised to transform precision neurovascular procedures with AI haptic feedback. We expect FDA approval in Q2 for the AI-augmented electrophysiology module.

Pipeline highlights include CardioFlow TAVR with 95% success rates; BioFix Advance Breakthrough Designation; NeuroPulse RF ablation first patients dosed; VitalFlow TAVR rollout; VitalSense CGM expansions. R&D at 12.5% of revenue targets robotics, neuromod, AI imaging—$300M investment yielding five 510(k)s filed. Real-world data: 22% faster procedures, 18% lower complications. We're scaling Smart Factory yields to 91% and advancing bioresorbables for PAD.

Next, Tom with some insights on our commercial strategy.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on driving commercial excellence and expanding our global reach. Our strategic partnerships are enabling us to access new markets and customer segments.

U.S. 65% revenue, 16% volumes via IDNs like HCA; China NMPA InnoValve Pro June, 50 reps for 35% growth; EMEA Fresenius renal pact to 15% share; APAC/EM $20M localization. Sales force 2,800 optimized via Salesforce, 12% rep productivity. Procedure Analytics Platform in 40% US sites +12% utilization. Value-based selling secured GPO uplifts, 65% hospital volumes renewed. Emerging: India/Brazil low-cost Trinity implants +15% volumes.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Tom. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: Press star then one. Our first question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee (JPMorgan):
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. On strategic priorities, can you expand on the $75M robotics investment and potential risks to Q2 FDA clearance?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, David. The $75M funds trials at 20 sites for the electrophysiology module, building on InnoBot Xi's 25% adoption growth. Real-world evidence supports 22% faster procedures, aligning with CMS IPPS. Risks to clearance are low—our 510(k) pathway is straightforward, mid-quarter target firm, with contingency for sequential launch.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Leerink Partners. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (Leerink Partners):
Great, thanks. Regarding procedure volumes, how sustainable is the 12-15% Q2 guide with Europe softness?

Maria Chen:
Emily, thanks. Sustainability comes from US 16% strength on CMS tailwinds and APAC 18% on China robotics. Europe 10% reflects NHS/NICE, but CE Mark live in 12 countries offsets. Upside from GLP-1 bariatrics and our analytics platform boosting utilization 12%. Modeling aligns with 8-10% FY25 global.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson (Goldman Sachs):
On SG&A leverage, what's the runway for 100-150 bps more in FY25, and impact of GenAI?

Tom Hargrove:
Mike, Efficiency 2.0 pillars—digitization like AI chatbots, rationalization, M&A synergies—already delivered 140 bps this quarter. GenAI in contract management unlocks $15-20M, Salesforce boosting virtual coverage 35%. Regional tailoring: US value-based cut CAC 18%, APAC digital training. Target 25.5-26% ratio sustainable.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong (Morgan Stanley):
Impressive mix shift to 72% consumables—how does this trend into FY25, and supply risks?

Raj Patel:
Lisa, thanks. 74% by YE25 from installed base +9%, utilization 72%, PrecisionNav 2.0 AI +17% efficiency. Supply derisked: dual-sourcing silicones/resins, Mexico nitinol, digital twin avoided $12M hits. Consumables 68% margins drive blended expansion, recurring covers 115% OpEx.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver sustainable growth.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
